steps.label: The 300 at the spring
steps.copy: God keeps only the three hundred men who lapped the water and sends the rest home.

steps.label: Torches and trumpets
steps.copy: At night the 300 blow trumpets and smash their jars, and the Midianite camp turns on itself and flees.

steps.label: Seizing the waters
steps.copy: The men of Ephraim take the waters as far as the Jordan and capture the commanders Oreb and Zeeb.

steps.label: Faint yet pursuing
steps.copy: Gideon's 300 cross the Jordan, exhausted, but the officials of Succoth refuse them bread.

steps.label: Penuel refuses too
steps.copy: The men of Penuel give the same answer.

steps.label: Overtaking at Karkor
steps.copy: He surprises the camp and captures the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna.

set.note: The text names the Kidron, the Mount of Olives, Bahurim and the Jordan crossing but not where on the Jordan they crossed. Bahurim is usually placed at Ras et-Tmim, just east of the Mount of Olives.

steps.label: Across the Kidron
steps.copy: Warned that Israel has turned to Absalom, David leaves the city, and the whole land weeps as the people cross the Kidron.

steps.label: Weeping up the Mount of Olives
steps.copy: David goes up the Mount of Olives weeping, his head covered and his feet bare.

steps.label: Shimei curses
steps.copy: At Bahurim, Shimei curses David and throws stones, and David will not let his men silence him.

steps.label: Across by night
steps.copy: Warned to hurry, David's whole company crosses the Jordan; by daybreak no one is left behind.

steps.label: Safe at Mahanaim
steps.copy: David reaches Mahanaim, where friends bring beds, food and supplies for the weary people.

steps.label: Down to Egypt
steps.copy: A severe famine drives Abram down to Egypt to live there for a while.

steps.label: Sarai taken
steps.copy: Sarai is taken into Pharaoh's house, and Abram is treated well for her sake.

steps.label: Sent away
steps.copy: After the Lord strikes Pharaoh's house with plagues, Pharaoh sends Abram away with all he has.

steps.label: Up into the Negev
steps.copy: Abram goes up out of Egypt into the Negev, very rich in livestock, silver and gold.

steps.label: Back to Bethel
steps.copy: He returns to the place between Bethel and Ai where he first built an altar, and calls on the Lord.

steps.label: Told to stay
steps.copy: In a famine the Lord tells Isaac not to go down to Egypt but to stay in the land, so he settles in Gerar.

steps.label: A hundredfold harvest
steps.copy: Isaac sows and reaps a hundredfold that year, and the Lord blesses him.

steps.label: Room at last
steps.copy: After quarrels over two wells, he digs Rehoboth: “At last the LORD has made room for us.”

steps.label: Up to Beersheba
steps.copy: He goes up to Beersheba, where the Lord appears to him, and he builds an altar.

steps.label: The camp of God
steps.copy: The angels of God meet him. “This is the camp of God,” he says, and names the place Mahanaim.

steps.label: Wrestling till dawn
steps.copy: By the Jabbok a man wrestles with Jacob until daybreak and renames him Israel.

steps.label: Face to face with Esau
steps.copy: Esau runs to meet him, embraces him, and they weep.

steps.label: Succoth
steps.copy: Jacob builds a house for himself and shelters for his livestock.

steps.label: On to Shechem
steps.copy: He comes safely to the city of Shechem and sets up an altar.

set.note: Midian and the mountain of God are both debated; they are shown at their traditional places.

steps.label: Leave to go
steps.copy: Jethro sends Moses off in peace to return to his people.

steps.label: The staff of God
steps.copy: Moses sets out for Egypt with his wife and sons, the staff of God in his hand.

steps.label: Aaron at the mountain
steps.copy: Sent by the Lord, Aaron meets him at the mountain of God and kisses him.

steps.label: Before the elders
steps.copy: They gather Israel's elders, who believe and bow down to worship.

set.note: The text names the regions Saul searched and 'the land of Zuph' but not Samuel's city. Ramah, Samuel's home (1 Samuel 7:17), is the usual guess.

points.modern: Er-Ram area, if Samuel's city was Ramah

steps.label: The lost donkeys
steps.copy: Saul and a servant pass through Ephraim, Shalishah, Shaalim and Benjamin but find nothing.

steps.label: The man of God
steps.copy: In the land of Zuph, the servant suggests they ask the seer in the town.

steps.label: Samuel's welcome
steps.copy: The Lord tells Samuel this is the man to lead Israel, and Samuel seats Saul at the head of the guests.

steps.label: The anointing
steps.copy: Samuel pours oil on Saul's head and kisses him.

steps.label: Home to Gibeah
steps.copy: God gives him a new heart, and Saul goes home to Gibeah with men whose hearts God had touched.

steps.label: Ziklag in ashes
steps.copy: Amalekites have burned the town and taken the families. David and his men weep until they have no strength left.

steps.label: Left at the brook
steps.copy: Two hundred stay behind, too exhausted to cross the Besor.

steps.label: All recovered
steps.copy: David strikes the raiders and recovers everything; nothing is missing, small or great.

steps.label: Shared alike
steps.copy: Back at the brook, David rules that those who stayed with the supplies share equally with those who fought.

steps.label: Gifts to Judah
steps.copy: Back in Ziklag, he sends part of the plunder to the elders of Judah.

steps.label: To the high place
steps.copy: Solomon offers a thousand burnt offerings at Gibeon.

steps.label: A dream at night
steps.copy: God says, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”

steps.label: A listening heart
steps.copy: Solomon asks for an understanding heart to judge the people and discern between good and evil.

steps.label: Back before the ark
steps.copy: He returns to Jerusalem and offers offerings before the ark.

steps.label: Praying for rain
steps.copy: Elijah crouches with his face between his knees.

steps.label: A cloud like a hand
steps.copy: The seventh time, his servant sees a cloud as small as a man's hand rising from the sea.

steps.label: The sky goes black
steps.copy: Heavy rain comes, and Ahab rides off to Jezreel.

steps.label: Outrunning the chariot
steps.copy: The hand of the Lord is on Elijah, and he runs ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.

steps.label: Up to Shechem
steps.copy: Rehoboam goes to Shechem, where all Israel has gathered to make him king.

steps.label: Lighten the yoke
steps.copy: The people ask him to ease the heavy yoke Solomon put on them.

steps.label: A harsher answer
steps.copy: Ignoring the elders, he threatens to make their yoke heavier still.

steps.label: To your tents
steps.copy: “To your tents, O Israel!” Israel rejects the house of David.

steps.label: Fleeing home
steps.copy: Israel stones his officer Adoram, and Rehoboam escapes by chariot to Jerusalem.

set.note: 2 Kings says Neco killed Josiah at Megiddo. 2 Chronicles 35:23-24 adds that archers wounded him there and he died after being brought to Jerusalem.

steps.label: Out of Babylon
steps.copy: On the first day of the first month, Ezra begins the journey up from Babylon.

steps.label: A fast at Ahava
steps.copy: Camped by the Ahava canal, Ezra calls a fast to ask God for a safe journey, ashamed to ask the king for soldiers.

steps.label: Protected on the road
steps.copy: God's hand keeps them from enemies and ambushes along the way, and they reach Jerusalem and rest three days.

steps.label: Treasure delivered
steps.copy: The silver, gold and vessels are weighed out in the house of God, and the returned exiles offer burnt offerings.

set.note: Every place on this route, and the crossing point itself, is debated. The stops follow the order Exodus gives.

steps.label: Out of Rameses
steps.copy: About six hundred thousand men on foot, besides women and children, set out from Rameses for Succoth.

steps.label: The long way round
steps.copy: God leads them by the wilderness road toward the Red Sea, not the short road through Philistine country.

steps.label: Camp at Etham
steps.copy: They camp at the edge of the wilderness, led by a pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.

steps.label: Hemmed in
steps.copy: God turns them back to camp by the sea at Pi-hahiroth, and Pharaoh thinks they are trapped.

steps.label: Through the sea
steps.copy: A strong east wind drives the sea back all night, and Israel walks through on dry ground.

steps.label: The waters return
steps.copy: The sea flows back over Pharaoh's chariots and horsemen, and the people fear the Lord and believe.

steps.label: Into the wilderness
steps.copy: Moses and Israel sing to the Lord, then go on three days into the wilderness of Shur without finding water.

steps.label: Up to the summit
steps.copy: Moses climbs from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, the top of Pisgah.

steps.label: The whole land shown
steps.copy: “This is the land that I swore to give Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,” the Lord says, “but you will not cross into it.”

steps.label: Moses dies in Moab
steps.copy: The servant of the Lord dies there, as the Lord had said.

steps.label: A hidden grave
steps.copy: He is buried in a valley in Moab, and no one knows the place to this day.

set.note: Which Kedesh is meant is debated: Kedesh in upper Galilee (shown) or a Kedesh near the Sea of Galilee. Jael's tent was near Kedesh (Judges 4:11).

steps.label: Barak called
steps.copy: Deborah sends for Barak at Kedesh: take ten thousand men to Mount Tabor. He will go only if she goes too.

steps.label: Up Mount Tabor
steps.copy: Ten thousand from Zebulun and Naphtali go up with Barak, and Sisera gathers his 900 iron chariots.

steps.label: Down from the mountain
steps.copy: “Arise,” Deborah tells him, and Barak charges down Tabor as the Lord throws Sisera's army into confusion.

steps.label: The Kishon sweeps them
steps.copy: Deborah's song: the ancient river Kishon swept them away.

steps.label: Jael's tent
steps.copy: Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael, near Kedesh, and dies there by her hand.

set.note: Genesis 16 doesn't name Abram's camp; he had settled by the oaks of Mamre at Hebron (Genesis 13:18). The spring lies 'between Kadesh and Bered' (16:14); its exact site is lost.

points.modern: Negev, between Kadesh and Bered (site lost)

steps.label: Fleeing Sarai
steps.copy: Treated harshly by Sarai, Hagar runs away.

steps.label: The angel at the spring
steps.copy: The angel of the Lord finds her by a spring on the way to Shur and tells her to return.

steps.label: The God who sees
steps.copy: She names the Lord: “You are the God who sees me.”

steps.label: The well named
steps.copy: The well is called Beer-lahai-roi, between Kadesh and Bered.

steps.label: The oak of Moreh
steps.copy: Abram passes through the land to the oak of Moreh at Shechem. The Canaanites are in the land.

steps.label: An altar at Shechem
steps.copy: The Lord appears: “I will give this land to your offspring.” Abram builds an altar.

steps.label: Between Bethel and Ai
steps.copy: He pitches his tent, builds an altar and calls on the name of the Lord.

steps.label: On toward the Negev
steps.copy: Abram journeys on by stages toward the Negev.
